subject: Post-call: Private Offer unit economics & marketplace mapping
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@novumai.com>, Lara Nguyen <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12 15:10 PDT
Subject: Post-call: Private Offer unit economics & marketplace mapping

Hi Samir / Lara — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before drafting the Private Offer (PO):

Summary of ask from NovumAI (Samir):
- Production forecast: ~50M tokens/month initially, scaling to ~150M in 6–9 months.
- Target list price goal: roughly $0.90 per 1k tokens equivalent (we discussed $900 / 1M tokens as a tidy unit to compare).
- Preferred path: AWS Private Offer (NovumAI is AWS-first) but want mapping to SKU/unit price so procurement can approve.

What Redwood needs from AWS (Lara):
- Mapping of the Redwood SKU(s) to an AWS Marketplace SKU and the mechanics of how unit pricing will show up on the PO (per 1M token equivalent or per-inference unit).
- Any platform/marketplace fees or minimum monthly commitments that would affect the effective $/1M tokens.

Attachments: attached token_breakdown_q1_2026.csv (Samir provided high-level usage shape used in the call).

Proposed next steps:
1) Lara confirms the SKU mapping & typical fees and returns the AWS pricing template.
2) Samir confirms committed monthly spend range for a PO (we discussed $45k–$60k/month as a narrow band for 50M tokens).
3) Redwood (me + Priyom) will draft the PO pricing proposal (targeting $900/1M tokens effective after marketplace fees) and circulate for signatures.

Can we get Lara's SKU mapping and a rough timeline (1–2 business days ideal)? Samir — can you confirm the committed monthly $ range by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@novumai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Nguyen <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-04-12 17:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private Offer unit economics & marketplace mapping

Thanks Rafael — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 50M/month is our conservative initial commit (pilot -> production). If the PO requires a dollar threshold instead, we're targeting $45k–$55k/month initially, with predictable step-ups tied to usage buckets.
- We want the PO to reflect a stable effective unit price (so our finance team can forecast). Marketplace fees are OK as long as the final $/1M token is <= $950.

I'll confirm the exact committed band tomorrow AM after double-checking procurement.

Samir
Head of Platform | NovumAI
samir@novumai.com

On Mon, Apr 12, 2026 at 3:10 PM Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samir / Lara — thanks for the call earlier...
From: Lara Nguyen <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Samir Shah <samir@novumai.com>
Date: 2026-04-13 09:22 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private Offer unit economics & marketplace mapping

Hi Rafael / Samir — appreciate the detailed note. Short answers: 

1) SKU mapping: we can expose a private-offer SKU that represents a unitized Redwoods inference usage line item. Typically the PO will reference a SKU and a unit price; the unit definition is seller-configurable (we can map to 1M-token bundles).
2) Fees: AWS marketplace fees vary by program — for commercial marketplace private offers there is a standard transaction fee. That fee will reduce the net amount the seller (Redwood) receives; the invoice to NovumAI will show the PO price. We can model both gross and net $/1M for procurement.
3) Technical: I'll attach our PO pricing template (aws_po_pricing_template.xlsx). Please fill in the SKU, the unit size (we suggest \"1M tokens\"), and the gross unit price.

If Redwood wants to target an effective $900/1M for NovumAI after fees, tell me the gross unit price you'd like visible on the PO and I'll confirm any marketplace deductions so the buyer sees the expected number.

I can turn around a draft private offer within 48 business hours once the SKU/unit price fields are provided and procurement confirms committed $ range.

Regards,
Lara Nguyen
AWS Marketplace — Commercial PM
aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com

[Attachment: aws_po_pricing_template.xlsx]
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@novumai.com>, Lara Nguyen <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-04-14 09:07 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private Offer unit economics & marketplace mapping

Adding internal math for transparency — pinging Marissa for pricing ops review: 

- Goal effective price: $900 / 1M tokens (net to customer after typical marketplace deductions).
- Marketplace deduction estimate (per AWS guidance): ~6–8% of gross (we'll use 7% as a working assumption).
- To net $900 at 7% fee, gross PO unit price = $900 / (1 - 0.07) = ~$967.74 -> round to $968 / 1M tokens as the PO line item.
- For NovumAI's 50M/month commit, monthly invoice at $968/1M gross = $48.4k gross; net to Redwood after fee ~ $45k.

Recommendation: propose PO gross unit price = $968 / 1M tokens; committed band = 50M/month for 3 months then review. If Samir confirms the $45k–$55k band, we can push the draft to Lara.

Priyom Das
Pricing & GTM Ops | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Thanks all — fast summary and next actions: 

Agreement in thread:
- NovumAI: target entry commit = 50M tokens / month (~$45k–$55k monthly).
- Redwood recommended gross PO unit price = $968 per 1M tokens (maps to ~$900 net after ~7% marketplace fees).
- Lara to prepare AWS Private Offer draft (SKU = REDWOOD-INFR-1M-TKN) using unit = 1M tokens and gross price = $968.

Next steps: 
1) Lara: please share the AWS PO draft when ready and include any buyer-side steps. ETA per thread: ~48 business hours.
2) Samir: please confirm committed monthly dollar band so procurement can approve and we can attach the PO to your SOW.
3) Redwood (Priyom + Rafael): we'll prepare a one-page summary and the internal pricing authorization (cc Marissa).

If that all looks correct I can kick-off the DocuSign flow/documentation after Lara sends the draft PO.

Best,
